title: Unit Type
concept: Unit is a type with exactly one value — () — representing 'nothing' or 'no meaningful value'.
why: Every expression must have a type, even ones that don't produce useful results. Unit fills that role cleanly.
syntax_ref:
() → The one and only value of type Unit

fn name() { }        // Implicitly returns Unit
fn name() -> Unit { }  // Explicitly returns Unit
tips: `()` is the one and only value of type `Unit`
Functions without `-> Type` implicitly return Unit
`io.println`, assignments, and semicolons all produce Unit
Unit is not an error — it's a deliberate 'nothing useful to return' type
common_mistakes: Trying to use the result of a void function: `let x = greet();` x will be ()
Confusing `()` (Unit value) with empty parentheses in function calls
Thinking Unit means 'error' — it means 'nothing to see here'
